claim_being_audited: The Actor claims that model certification is supportable because aggregate performance passes deployment criteria, but only if the small-business support slice weakness and its sampling uncertainty are explicitly disclosed in the model card, since no approved mitigation removes exposure.
specific_concerns: The available record to this role is only the Actor's summary, not the underlying admissible documents, so the threshold calculations and mitigation status are not independently verifiable.

The recommended action is `certify_model`, but the policy allows certification only if the material weakness is actually disclosed or exposure is removed by approved mitigation; the current record does not show that the disclosure has been made.
The Actor asserts the small-business support slice may materially affect a contractual customer segment, but the materiality basis is not directly shown in the evidence available to this role.
The packet supports a conditional certification posture more clearly than an unconditional certification action.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant, rather than merely potentially compliant if disclosure is added.
That the small-business support slice materiality predicate is fully established from the evidence available to this role.
That no approved mitigation exists, beyond the Actor's characterization of the record.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BMCARD-045-A through BMCARD-045-E, especially the aggregate threshold, slice thresholds, and mitigation/disclosure status.
Provide the current model-card text or approval artifact showing the small-business support weakness and uncertainty are explicitly disclosed.
Provide the document establishing why the small-business support slice is a materially affected protected or contractual customer segment.
Provide any approval record confirming whether a mitigation was reviewed and whether it removes deployment exposure.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if material weaknesses are disclosed or an approved mitigation removes deployment exposure.
Aggregate pass rates can support launch readiness but do not erase subgroup weaknesses.
Small-sample uncertainty can reduce confidence but does not convert an unresolved materiality issue into a clean certification.
An action should not be treated as compliant when a required disclosure or approval link is only proposed rather than evidenced.
